The Ruins of Hoth Akhbir

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-size:9.0pt;font-family:"CenturyGothic","sans-serif"; mso-fareast-font-family:"맑은고딕";mso-bidi-font-family:"TimesNewRoman"; color:black;mso-themecolor:text1">While at the zenith of their power, before the goblin wars ([24.02](/wiki/24-02/)), the [dwarven](/wiki/dwarves/) dictators ordered the construction of five great fortresses ([26.01](/wiki/26-01/)) but only one ([33.00](/wiki/33-00/)) remains in dwarven hands today. The construction of Hoth Akhbir was especially ambitious for it sought to extend dwarven power all the way to the western coast. Maybe it would have done so, but its construction was never completed. </span>

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-size:9.0pt;font-family:"CenturyGothic","sans-serif"; mso-fareast-font-family:"맑은고딕";mso-bidi-font-family:"TimesNewRoman"; color:black;mso-themecolor:text1">While the [orcish](/wiki/orcs/) and dwarven work crews were still hard at work raising the stones of the towers of Hoth Akhbir ever higher, a [stone giant](/wiki/stone-giants/) war band fell upon the work site, heaving great blocks of stone at the surprised engineers. It was all the work of [Najir Dum](/wiki/najir-dum/). This goblin hero had acquired an enchanted flute of elven make and used it to draw the [gnomish](/wiki/gnomes/) children out of the walls of the castle of [the Mountain King](/wiki/the-mountain-king/). When their parents came wailing to him asking for their children back, Najir Dum said that he would be happy to oblige if they would steal the harp of the Mountain King in return. </span>

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-size:9.0pt;font-family:"CenturyGothic","sans-serif"; mso-fareast-font-family:"맑은고딕";mso-bidi-font-family:"TimesNewRoman"; color:black;mso-themecolor:text1">The gnomes sniveled and screamed but in the end they agreed and the great golden harp passed into Najir Dum’s hands. Then, riding on the back of a great [bat](/wiki/bats/), he took the harp southwards and secreted it within the half-built walls of Hoth Akhbir. Najir Dum made sure that the Mountain King learned of where he harp could be found and that was the end for many dwarves, orcs and gnomes (once the giants learned of the gnomes' role in the theft their wrath was terrible).</span>

<span lang="EN-US" style="font-size:9.0pt;font-family:"CenturyGothic","sans-serif"; mso-fareast-font-family:"맑은고딕";mso-bidi-font-family:"TimesNewRoman"; color:black;mso-themecolor:text1">This is only one of the many stories the goblins still tell of the cunning of Najir Dum but they are not the only ones who remember the fate of Hoth Akhbir. The dwarven monastery ([03.04](/wiki/03-04/)) was later built out of its fallen stones and even today the dwarven brothers come here to drag away more of its stones.</span>

With Not a Soul to Hear

The ruins of Hoth Akbir are soaked by a constant downpour that helps feed rivers that run both west and east. But the water that falls from the cloud is not rain but rather a decanter of endless water that was left behind in the shattered ruins of the castle of one of the pirate kings that lies on a cloud that stays forever unmoving above Hoth Akbir.

Hooks:

  • A decanter of endless water seems like a useful thing to have, why hasn’t anyone taken it?
